providers.title: An exact Boolean circuit for the Forrelation function
providers.scope: For fixed k >= 2 and every power of four m there is a Boolean circuit with gates of at most two inputs and size at most C_k m (log m)^2 with two outputs d, b: d = 1 exactly if the k-fold Forrelation function with thresholds delta = 2^(-5k) and delta/2 is defined on the input, and then b is its value.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A winner at a given address is recognized by local tests
providers.scope: For the function F_(k,m), a column i and an address s: i wins at s if and only if K = m + (m-1) + r(S+2) tests pass, each of which reads at most log2(m) + 1 input bits.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Measurements during a computation can be deferred
providers.scope: A quantum query procedure given by a finite tree of unitary maps, queries and measurements with outcome-dependent continuation, with at most T queries on every path, is simulated by a query algorithm with T queries (unitary maps, queries, one measurement at the end) with the same output probabilities on every input.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Read queries at computed positions
providers.scope: For a function loc from the labels of a register to the positions, the map |c, b> -> |c, b + x_loc(c)> is obtained with one query and permutation maps, with the index and bit registers restored.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Phase queries and conditional queries
providers.scope: The map |c> -> (-1)^(x_loc(c)) |c>, and the read query applied only for c in a given subset, are each obtained with two queries and one ancilla bit that is restored.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Decision trees in superposition
providers.scope: For decision trees A_c of depth at most q, c in a finite set: a query circuit with q queries maps |c>|0>|y> to |c>|answers>|y + A_c(x)> for all c and x.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The rotation of amplitude amplification
providers.scope: For a preparation A with success probability sin^2(theta) in (0,1), successful state g and unsuccessful state b, and G = A S_0 A^(-1) S: G^l A|0> = sin((2l+1) theta) g + cos((2l+1) theta) b.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Amplification with a fixed successful state
providers.scope: For a preparation with c queries, 0 < gamma <= 1/2 and 0 < eta < 1/2 there is a procedure with at most 88 c gamma^(-1/2) log2(1/eta) queries on every path that fails always if p = 0, fails with probability at most eta if p >= gamma, and whenever it succeeds holds the successful state g of the preparation.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Forrelation test
providers.scope: A preparation with k phase queries has success probability Phi(z_1, ..., z_k)^2, where Phi = u^T D_(z_1) H D_(z_2) H ... H D_(z_k) u.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Forrelation function with bounded error
providers.scope: For 0 < eta < 1/2 a query circuit with at most 384 k 2^(10k) log2(1/eta) queries, independent of m, has an answer bit that equals the Forrelation function with probability at least 1 - eta on every input of its domain.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A tournament for probabilistic comparisons
providers.scope: Let a comparison circuit with c queries have win probabilities a_ij with a_ij + a_ji = 1. With T = ceil(log2(1000 m)) and eps = 1/(1000 T), a procedure with at most 63 c sqrt(m) T^2 log2(1000 T) queries returns a list of at most T candidates that contains every candidate i with a_ij >= 1 - eps for all j, with probability at least 1 - 3/1000. No transitivity is assumed.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The quantum query complexity of F_(k,m)
providers.scope: For every k >= 2 there is C_k with Q(F_(k,m)) <= C_k sqrt(m) (log2 m)^4 for all powers of four m >= 4. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Guessing the answers of several independent inputs
providers.scope: Let every decision tree of depth at most L compute P with probability at most beta under mu. A decision tree on r independent inputs with law mu that makes at most L queries to each input, with adaptive interleaving and independent side information, outputs all r values of P with probability at most beta^r.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The randomized query complexity of F_(k,m)
providers.scope: Assume the hypothesis (BS) (Bansal and Sinha's lower bound for Forrelation; not proved in the programme). For k >= 2 and all large powers of four m: R(F_(k,m)) > floor(m L / 100) with L = floor(m^(1-1/k) / (log2 m)^2).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The adversary bound with nonnegative weights
providers.scope: For a nonconstant total Boolean function f and a nonzero symmetric matrix Gamma >= 0 indexed by inputs with Gamma_xy = 0 when f(x) = f(y): Q(f) >= c_0 ||Gamma|| / max_i ||Gamma_i||, c_0 = (3 - 2 sqrt 2)/6, where Gamma_i keeps the entries with x_i different from y_i.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Block sensitivity and the sensitivity graph against quantum queries
providers.scope: For nonconstant total f: bs(f) <= Q(f)^2 / c_0^2 and lambda(f) <= Q(f) / c_0, where lambda(f) is the norm of the adjacency matrix of the sensitivity graph.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Degree and the sensitivity graph (Huang)
providers.scope: For every total Boolean function: deg(f) <= lambda(f)^2. In particular a set of more than half of the vertices of the d-cube induces a graph whose adjacency matrix has norm at least sqrt(d).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deterministic queries, block sensitivity and degree
providers.scope: For every total Boolean function: D(f) <= bs(f) deg(f).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The quartic bound
providers.scope: For every total Boolean function: R(f) <= D(f) <= c_0^(-4) Q(f)^4 <= 1.5 * 10^6 Q(f)^4. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
